answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each trading identity to lock a stake and build reputation through work with known peers. Random committees of older stake-backed identities audit claims and slash deposits when colluding clones disagree. Creating many juniper identities multiplies locked capital and audit exposure: the attacker must fund each fake, establish its history, and risk losing every stake, while honest agents anchor trust to costly continuity rather than names on a ledge.
